COVID-19 poses a clear negative shock to near-term activity and the outlook, but the FOMC’s swift cut to the ZLB, large-scale Treasury and MBS purchases, expanded repos, and dollar swap lines align with the credit-channel/financial-accelerator literature (e.g., Oliner and Rudebusch; Gertler and Gilchrist), which helps reduce external finance premia and support investment. With inflation expectations broadly anchored in an inflation-targeting framework (Svensson), these measures can mitigate liquidity-trap risks and temper the downturn, suggesting significant policy offsets to otherwise adverse conditions.
